newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai soymeal price up on weak baht, corn steady.
newsitem.headline: Thai soymeal price up on weak baht, corn steady.

text.p: Thai soymeal prices edged up this week as demand rose amid a weakening baht against the dollar, while corn prices were mostly steady, trade sources said on Tuesday.

There have been active enquiries in the market for soymeal. But the only deal heard in the market this week was a purchase of 20,000 tonnes of optional origin soymeal from South America for February shipment.
The price was quoted around $309 per tonne c&f Bangkok.
Soymeal was quoted around 9.40 baht per kg ($0.37) versus 9.20 baht a week ago, trade sources said.
"The strong dollar makes the product more expensive in baht terms. High demand also supported prices," said one trader.
Corn prices were mostly steady at 4.25 baht per kg, barely changed from last week in modest trade.
There was market talks that U.S. corn bought by one major animal feed producer here was coming to this area. But since the deal was on an fob basis, the exact destination was not known.
"I guess the buyer is looking for loopholes to bring the corn in. It's on fob because if there is any problem, they can shift the product to other destinations," said another trader.
In a move to help local corn farmers, the govenment recently decided to delay the date for zero-tariff corn imports from February 20-June 30 set originally.
